title: Ticket sheet sections as tabs instead of jump links
description: User feedback 2026-10-18: the sheet's jump links (Overview, Stage history, Sessions, Agent notes) will get long as sections grow (devserve preview is next). Replace them with tab headers and show one section at a time. Active tab lives in the URL (tab param beside the open ticket) so refresh, back and shared links keep it; default Overview. Tab headers may carry counts (status, not prose). Streams keep updating while a tab is hidden. Same component on Initiatives and Pull requests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tabs replace the jump-link nav on the ticket sheet on both pages
- [ ] Active tab in the URL; refresh and back restore it; unknown tab falls back to Overview
- [ ] Hidden tabs still receive live updates (switching shows current history/sessions/notes)
- [ ] Keyboard: arrow keys move between tabs, focus visible
- [ ] Browser-checked light and dark, narrow and wide; screenshots looked at
- [ ] mix precommit green

title: Flaky: Initiatives first visit sometimes redirects in LiveView tests
description:
## What to build
Found during bb-c2w.9 review (2026-10-18): a recorded transient precommit failure. The first bare visit to Initiatives can redirect inside a LiveView test.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Reproduce: test/board_web/live/initiatives_live_test.exs:227 sometimes fails with {:error, {:redirect, %{to: "http://www.example.com/"}}} on live(conn, "/")
- [ ] Root cause found (FilterRestore first-bare-route redirect racing the session/localStorage seed is the suspect) and fixed in the code, not by retrying the test
- [ ] The test passes 50 runs in a row with random seeds
close_reason: Cause: WSL clock rollback vs Plug.Crypto future-token check. Test-only signing allowance; 50 focused + 10 full randomized runs green; documented. Merged.

title: Preview servers from the ticket sheet, tied to the ticket's stage
description:
## What to build
User direction (2026-10-18): worktree preview servers are launched from the board on demand, from the ticket they belong to, and cleaned up when that ticket moves forward, so there are no orphan servers. The ticket sheet (bb-c2w.6) is the surface for the controls.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The ticket sheet shows a Preview control for a ticket with a session worktree: start, open URL, follow logs, stop
- [ ] Start runs the worktree app as a transient systemd user service through devserve (skills initiative sk-9ro); never started automatically
- [ ] The preview lifecycle is a Board.Fsm machine; moving the ticket past review (merged, done, abandoned) stops and cleans up its preview, including its dev database
- [ ] Previews with no ticket or a vanished worktree are listed and can be stopped; nothing is left running unowned
- [ ] Blocked on devserve existing (sk-9ro, skills repo): check it before starting

title: Curated view buttons instead of filter dropdowns
description:
## What to build
User feedback on the demo (2026-10-18): dropdown filters feel heavy. Replace them with a curated set of preset view buttons, with the full filters tucked into a normally closed advanced section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A row of view buttons replaces the dropdown row: Open (default: everything not closed), In flight (dispatched, building, reported, in_review), Stale, All; search stays visible; project still comes from the sidebar
- [ ] Views are data: named filter presets shipped in the defaults, curated in board.toml [[views]] (add, remove, reorder), validated like columns (unknown stage or status names are load errors), hot-reloaded
- [ ] Advanced filters (beads status, type, label) in a collapsed Filters section, closed by default; open/closed remembered per browser; any advanced filter active shows on the closed section header as a count
- [ ] URL carries the view (?view=stale&project=...); existing URL, back/forward and restore-on-return behaviour keeps working; old ?status=/type=/label= links still apply as advanced filters
- [ ] Disclosure and view selection on Board.Fsm where they have states; LiveView tests; screenshots light and dark looked at; no explanatory copy
close_reason: Merged 1d2e8de: view presets in config, button group, collapsed advanced filters; 167 tests

title: Durable filters and sidebar project filter
description:
## What to build
User feedback from the first demo (2026-10-18): filter state is lost when navigating to Settings and back, and the sidebar project list should act as the project filter with the active one highlighted.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Initiatives filters (project, beads status, type, label, search, stale) live in the URL query; back/forward and reload keep them; a copied URL reproduces the view
- [ ] Leaving for Settings (or any page) and returning restores the last filters, kept per browser

description:
## What to build
The proof the MVP does its job: a normal day of work keeps the board right without anyone updating it by hand (spec Why). Not a build ticket; a verification pass with fixes filed as fallout.

title: Forge boundary and read-only PR panel
description:
## What to build
Each project's open change requests in stack order, linked to their beads, behind a forge boundary so another forge later is an adapter plus a config line (spec Decision 9).

## Interfaces
Consumes: apply_event (5). Produces: the Board.Forge behaviour and capabilities, consumed by the merge action (9).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Board.Forge behaviour: change requests (number, title, source/target branch, head sha, draft, checks, mergeable), list, merge with expected head, retarget, declared capabilities
- [ ] Fake in-memory forge; GitHub adapter (token from gh at boot, Req); one contract suite run against both (GitHub on recorded responses)
- [ ] PR sync, stack order, detached bases, linking by bead id in title/branch/body
- [ ] Observed cr_opened / cr_closed / cr_merged move linked tickets per the stage machine
- [ ] form-engine real stack shows in order, linked, read-only; nothing mergeable whose base is not the default branch (check 9)
- [ ] Config names the forge per repo; repos without a remote show no panel

title: Agent API and the board CLI
description:
## What to build
How agents keep the board current without ever being blocked by it (spec Decisions 3, 8, 11). The verbs are the contract the skills wiring (tickets 11, 12) builds on.

## Interfaces
Consumes: apply_event and the machines' events (5).
Produces: the board CLI verbs and the HTTP API. Consumed by the skills-repo tickets.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Localhost API with a bearer token kept under ~/.ssh; claimed events only (observed events cannot be posted)
- [ ] board CLI: verbs for every claimed ticket event and the draft-epic events; repo resolved from the bead id prefix, drafts by slug and working directory or --project; --json
- [ ] Out-of-order claim exits 3 printing stage and allowed events; it is logged as invalid (check 4)
- [ ] App down: event written to the spooled-events table, exit 0 with a warning; replayed on boot; Postgres down too: warning, exit 0 (check 5)
- [ ] Each CLI write pings a sync of that repo
notes: 2026-10-17 (user): add the verb board attach <ticket> --epic <epic> (and detach), writing the board-side epic link; used for cross-repo tickets such as sk-5o2/sk-osj under bb-c2w.
close_reason: Merged de0b961: agent API and board CLI, Postgres spool, hermetic per-checkout test DBs; token path only from BOARD_TOKEN_FILE; 247 tests

title: Always on: one release, two systemd user units (web, worker)
description:
## What to build
The board runs whenever agents do, without anyone starting it (spec Decision 1).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One mix release; a role setting selects web, worker or all (dev/tests)
- [ ] Two user unit files (beads-board-web, beads-board-worker) with Restart=always, env from the house locations, journald logs; install and update steps in the README; the user installs them (ask-first)
- [ ] Web runs no reader, scheduler or watcher; worker runs no endpoint; live updates reach the browser across the two nodes through Postgres
- [ ] Survives killing either process and a WSL restart; up before agents start
notes: Built and merged c18c59f: units, env examples, README steps, release smoke test. Stays open until the user installs the units and it survives a WSL restart (acceptance).

comments.author: Ryan Messner

title: Merge action with stack and head-sha guards
description:
## What to build
The one write the board makes: merging the bottom of a stack, safely, with confirmation (spec Decision 10).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Merge-action machine (idle, confirming, merging, retargeting, merged, failed) on Board.Fsm; guards read forge capabilities
- [ ] Rules enforced in the job: bottom of stack only, not draft, checks passing or absent, mergeable, merge commit, expected head sha; audit table
- [ ] Confirm dialog names CR, target, head sha, linked beads and the follow-up retarget; then the child retargets; no branch deletion
- [ ] Ask the user before creating the scratch GitHub repo; live run there: top of stack refused, bottom merged at the confirmed sha, child retargeted, moved head refused, ticket goes merged and the bd close suggestion shows (check 8)
- [ ] Recorded responses from the live run refresh the contract fixtures
close_reason: Live run on rpmessner/beads-board-scratch passed every check (refusals, merge commit at confirmed head, retarget, branches kept, observed merged); real fixtures recorded. Merged 88a4220.

title: App shell, config and beads read model
description:
## What to build
The app boots, knows which repos to read from its config, and keeps a live, droppable projection of every configured beads repo, without ever disturbing an agent's bd write (spec Decisions 1-5). Settings shows what it sees. Covers acceptance checks 1, 2, 2a, 10 and the precommit half of 11.

## Interfaces
Produces: the beads projection (repos, beads, edges, comments) and its change broadcasts; the config API (columns, repos, backfill defaults). Consumed by tickets 5-8.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Phoenix + LiveView + Oban + Postgres (versions as gw2), bound to 127.0.0.1; Fluxon wired from env vars; mix precommit includes a guard that fails on license material or local operator paths
- [ ] board.toml (global plus untracked local override, defaults shipped) loaded, validated (unknown stage names are errors), hot-reloaded; a bad edit keeps the last good config
- [ ] bd export sync per repo with polling, CLI-ping hook point, 5-minute sweep, hash skip, and the probe read rule; unreachable repos shown, never blocking others; unknown bd values never crash
- [ ] Every configured repo synced; counts equal bd list --all; a bd note shows in the projection within the target
- [ ] Probe write loop against the running sync: zero failed agent writes
- [ ] Settings view (repos, sync state, config source and validation, reload, unconfigured repos found on disk) built only after the revised mockup is approved
- [ ] The implementing agent may split this into 4a/4b across sessions; record the split in a bead note
notes:
4a merged b594094: config layer, reload machine, hygiene guard, Board.Stage promoted. 4b remains: runtime (Oban, Postgres projection, Fluxon), bd reader per the probe rule, Settings view.
4b-1 merged b3845feedd834f4c5651ca6d22155638a47d06fa: runtime, export decoding, journal lock check, projection. Remaining (4b-2): reader and scheduler machines, config watcher through Oban, sync status and broadcasts, Fluxon, Settings view, real-repo acceptance.
4b-2 merged 3f0de68e528ba3ae23ec935d36ddb89ae83cc70f: read/schedule machines, roles, Postgres events. Remaining (4b-3): effect executors (bd subprocess, scheduler, path resolver, admission), config watcher wiring, sync status, Fluxon, Settings, real-repo acceptance.
close_reason: Merged 8239605 across 4a/4b-1/4b-2/4b-3: config, runtime, bd sync per the probe rule, roles, Fluxon, Settings; acceptance 855 writes zero failures, 0.74 s freshness, counts match; 124 tests

title: Initiatives view: epics as the spine
description:
## What to build
The board's home: every initiative across projects and where it stands, with the work under it, the fallout it produced, and the few orphans (user: work derives from epics). Introduces the overlay and the two machines everything else moves.

## Interfaces
Consumes: Board.Fsm (3), the projection and config (4).
Produces: Board.Stage and Board.Epic event names and states, Board.Overlay.apply_event, the epic tree query. Consumed by tickets 6, 7, 8.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Ticket-stage and epic machines declared with Board.Fsm exactly as spec Decisions 7 and 8; generated docs committed
- [ ] Overlay tables and apply_event (lock, step, record event, run effects in one transaction, broadcast after commit); invalid claims logged
- [ ] Backfill: closed beads done, open queued; beads epics ticketed or done; epics never get a ticket stage
- [ ] Epic tree derived: planned (parent-child, any depth), fallout (discovered-from under the epic), orphans
- [ ] Home view per the approved mockup: epic rows with derived stage, progress, histogram, fallout count; drafts on top; Unplanned lane; filters
- [ ] fe-813 and fe-lwp match bd; a discovered-from ticket shows as fallout; an orphan shows in Unplanned (check 2b)
- [ ] Events applied from iex move rows live
notes: 2026-10-17 (user, mockup review): fallout wins over parent-child; cross-repo tickets join an epic via board-side links (overlay table, set by board attach); sub-epics are expandable rows with rolled-up counts; Unplanned collapsed, grouped by project. See spec Decisions 8 and 13.
close_reason: Merged c18c59f: overlay, stage/epic machines, epic tree, Initiatives home; acceptance 2b on real repos; 143+ tests

title: Board.Fsm: the house Elixir state-machine DSL
description:
## What to build
The macro DSL every stateful feature in the board is declared with (spec Decision 6), as a library with its own tests. Concepts match form-engine's Zig kit (rows, groups, any, stay, explicit ignore/invalid, compile-time coverage); syntax is Elixir declarations. No :gen_statem in the MVP. Includes the project scaffold it needs to compile and test if ticket 4 has not landed yet (coordinate: whichever lands first owns the mix project).

## Interfaces
Produces: `use Board.Fsm` and the generated step/3, __fsm__/1, to_mermaid/0, matrix/0. Consumed by the stage and epic machines (ticket 5) and the merge-action machine (ticket 9).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Declarations as calls: initial, state (enter/exit), group, event (claimed/observed), guard, effects, transition, ignore, invalid; row resolution by specificity then declaration order
- [ ] Every compile check in spec Decision 6 has a fixture that fails to compile with its documented message
- [ ] step/3 pure and total; effects as data; {:error, {:invalid, state, event}} for invalid pairs
- [ ] Mermaid and full matrix generated by a mix task; a test fails when the committed doc differs
- [ ] Property test: random event sequences never raise; observed events never invalid where the option is on
- [ ] mix precommit passes
close_reason: 947b9c8: Board.Fsm DSL with all Decision 6 compile checks (exact-message fixtures), pure step/3, generated Mermaid/matrix goldens, stage and epic machines as fixtures; 50 tests, 4 properties; coordinator reran gates

title: Probe: can the board's beads reads break an agent's bd write?
description:
## What to build
The answer to the riskiest unknown before the reader exists: embedded Dolt is opened by every bd process, and even bd export rewrites store files, so a board read could collide with an agent's write. The spec's rule (Decision 5): the board is failure tolerant and never interrupts an agent's bd write. This probe finds out which case we are in and fixes the read rule ticket 4 implements.

## Interfaces
Produces: the read rule (written decision with evidence), consumed by the beads read model.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] On a scratch copy of a real embedded-store repo, a bd export loop runs against a loop of agent-style writes (create, update, note, close) for 10 minutes
- [ ] Failed writes, failed reads and their errors counted and recorded
- [ ] Read rule chosen and written in the repo docs: normal reads, skip while a write is visible (how it is detected), or slower polling with the 30 s freshness target
- [ ] No real repo touched
notes: Correction: merged in 5fb8e9e (the close reason's cc62dcb was the pre-merge head).
close_reason: cc62dcb: zero failed agent writes in 4,155 under concurrent exports (two runs, four scenarios); read rule in docs/probe-bd-concurrency.md

title: beads-board MVP: an epic-first work board for every local beads repo
description:
# beads-board MVP: spec

Status: draft for approval, 2026-10-17. Design detail and rationale live in `docs/design.md` (the design pass); the mockup's source is in `docs/mockup/` (live: https://claude.ai/artifact/BwE6JCfLAQMnSgdEDSSdNg). The mockup predates the epic-first decision and is revised before the build (Decision 13). Where this spec and the design disagree, this spec wins.

## Goal

A local web board organised around epics (major features and initiatives) that shows each epic's stage from idea to shipped, the planned tickets and fallout under it, the few orphan one-offs, and each project's open change requests, kept current by agents through the house skills.

## Why

The user's work is driven by epics: a feature set or initiative drives all the planned work under it, plus the fallout found along the way; orphan bug fixes exist but are the exception. They want to see where each initiative stands without being inside a coding session: which are still ideas or specs, which are being built, what each ticket under them is doing, and what PR stack is open per project. Agents (Claude Code coordinator, pi build sessions) keep it current as a side effect of the workflow they already follow, so the board can be trusted at a glance. Success: after a normal day of speccing, dispatching and merging, the board matches reality without anyone updating it by hand.

## Non-goals

- Writing to beads in any form (create, update, close, notes, labels). Beads is read-only; the board suggests `bd` commands, it never runs them. Two-way sync is a later project; the MVP only keeps the path open.
- Adding any file, hook or field to the beads repos. A board that needs repo cruft has failed even if it works.
- Editing ticket content in the UI. It is a dashboard plus a merge action.
- Launching, steering or killing pi/tmux sessions; touching worktrees or running local git.
- Forge adapters other than GitHub; creating PRs; squash or rebase merges; reviewing diffs; deleting branches.
- Starting Dolt servers or migrating repos out of server mode.
- Multi-user, remote hosting, auth beyond a local token.

## Decisions

1. **Stack** (agent call, from design): Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.1, Oban on Postgres 16, the same versions gw2 pins; bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runs as a release under a user systemd unit so it is up whenever agents are.
2. **Fluxon UI** (user): Fluxon's components and default theme (light and dark). The license is read from environment variables set in the untracked shell-local file; nothing that identifies the license material enters the repo, and `mix precommit` checks for it.
3. **Where data lives** (user: Postgres for all of the app's storage, no flat files, SQLite only if unavoidable, which it is not): a field lives with its writer. Beads owns ticket content (read through `bd export`, projected into droppable tables). Postgres owns every process fact beads does not know (stages, events, sessions, agent notes, change-request links, merge audit, draft epics) and the CLI's offline queue (a spooled-events table the CLI writes directly when the web app is down; Postgres runs as a service independent of the app). The only non-database files are the hand-edited TOML config (settings, not data) and the API token, which is a secret and lives with the other secrets under `~/.ssh`.
4. **Config file** (agent call, user floated): one global `board.toml` under the user's config dir, kept in dotfiles with home-relative paths, plus an untracked local override file; defaults ship in the app. It lists repos (path, forge, forge repo, colour, enabled), board columns as groups of stages, backfill defaults, swimlane default, stale-session threshold, per-epic display options. It may name stages, never define them: unknown stage names are a load error. Hot reload on change; a bad edit keeps the last good config and shows the error. No per-repo config file.
5. **Reading beads** (agent call; failure rule is the user's): one `bd export` per repo per sync; change noticed by polling cheap file signals every few seconds, pings from the `board` CLI, and a 5-minute sweep; an unchanged export hash is a no-op. A repo whose store cannot be opened (we_go_next_dev today) shows as unreachable, never blocks the others. Unknown bd statuses or types render as grey badges, never crash. **The board is failure tolerant and never interrupts an agent's `bd` write** (user): a failed or contended read is retried later and never surfaced as an error to agents; if the concurrency probe (first ticket) shows reads can break writes, the reader skips while a write is visible or reads less often, and the freshness target relaxes from 5 s to 30 s. The store is never copied or written by the board.
6. **State-machine DSL** (user): every stateful feature is a machine declared with a house Elixir macro DSL, as function-call-style declarations (`initial`, `state`, `group`, `event`, `guard`, `effects`, `transition`, `ignore`, `invalid`). Compile-time errors for: undeclared names, missing or duplicate `initial`, guards without a function, uncovered (state, event) pairs, all-guarded pairs, duplicate rows, dead rows, unreachable states, effects on ignore/invalid rows, and (per machine option) observed events declared invalid. `step/3` is pure and total, returns `{next_state, effects}` with effects as data, or `{:error, {:invalid, state, event}}`. Mermaid diagram and full matrix are generated and held to a committed golden file. `:gen_statem` only for a machine that needs timeouts; none in the MVP. Lives in this repo until a second Elixir repo needs it.
7. **Ticket stage machine** (agent call, from design): states and events as below. Claimed events come from agents or the UI and are refused when out of order (the API answers with the current stage and the allowed events); observed events are facts from beads or the forge and are never refused.

   | From | Event | To | Effects |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | queued | dispatch (claimed) | dispatched | record session |
   | dispatched, building | dispatch [new session] | dispatched | record session, note re-dispatch |
   | dispatched, building | progress | building | append progress |
   | reported .. merged | progress | stay | append progress |
   | dispatched, building | report | reported | record report |
   | reported | review | in_review | |
   | in_review | request_changes | building | append finding |
   | in_review | commit | committed | record commit |
   | committed | commit | stay | record commit |
   | any live stage | abandon | abandoned | |
   | abandoned | revive | queued | |
   | queued .. committed | cr_opened (observed) | pr_open | link change request |
   | pr_open, merged | cr_opened | stay | link |
   | pr_open | cr_closed [another open CR] | stay | unlink |
   | pr_open | cr_closed | committed | unlink |
   | pr_open | cr_merged | merged | record merge; on entering merged, suggest the `bd close` |
   | pr_open | bead_closed | done | flag "closed with open CR" |
   | any live stage | bead_closed | done | |
   | done | bead_reopened | queued | |
   | everything else: observed events ignored, claimed events invalid | | | |

   Live stages: queued, dispatched, building, reported, in_review, committed, pr_open, merged. Every transition also broadcasts. Tickets seen for the first time are backfilled (closed to done, open to queued) as recorded backfill events.
8. **Epic machine** (user: epics get their own tracked state, with the coordinator's recommendation): epics have a stage of their own for the stretch before tickets exist; after that their state is derived from their children (progress closed/total plus a stage histogram), not tracked twice.

   | From | Event | To | Effects |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | (new draft) | create (claimed) | idea | record draft title, spec link |
   | idea | start_spec | speccing | |
   | speccing | approve_spec | spec_approved | record spec link |
   | spec_approved | ticket [beads epic id given] | ticketed | link the beads epic |
   | idea, speccing, spec_approved | abandon | abandoned | |
   | abandoned | revive | idea | |
   | any | bead_epic_closed (observed) | done | |
   | done | bead_epic_reopened (observed) | ticketed | |
   | everything else: observed ignored, claimed invalid | | | |

   Draft epics live only in the overlay until `ticket` links them to a beads epic. A draft is keyed by a slug (`draft:<slug>`); its project is the configured repo containing the caller's working directory, or `--project`; its spec link is the spec file `/tight-spec` writes. Only project-size specs create a draft. `/to-tickets` finds the draft by slug and sends `ticket` with the new beads epic id (agent call). Beads epics the board first sees are backfilled to `ticketed` (or `done` when closed). From `ticketed` on, the epic's displayed stage is derived from its children: building once any child is past queued, shipping once all open children are committed or later, shipped when all are closed. Beads epics never get a ticket stage.

   **What sits under an epic** (user: work derives from epics): its planned tickets (parent-child, any depth) and its fallout (tickets linked `discovered-from` to anything under the epic), shown apart. Tickets with no epic above them and no `discovered-from` link are orphans.
9. **Forge boundary** (user): a forge behaviour with change requests (number, title, source and target branch, head sha, draft, checks, mergeable), list, merge-with-expected-head and retarget, and declared capabilities (head guard, retarget). The merge machine's guards read capabilities: without a head guard the board re-reads the head immediately before merging and says the guard is weaker; without retarget it stops after the merge and shows the manual step. The MVP ships the GitHub adapter (token from the logged-in `gh` at boot, HTTP through Req) and an in-memory fake forge for tests. Config names the forge per repo.
10. **Merge safety** (agent call): bottom of a stack only; not draft; checks passing or absent; mergeable; merge commits only; expected head sha; confirmation dialog names the CR, target, head sha, linked beads and the follow-up retarget; then the child is retargeted onto the default branch; no branch deletion. All rules enforced in the job, not only the UI; every merge recorded in an audit table. Merge action machine (UI): idle, confirming, merging, retargeting, merged, failed.
11. **Agent tools** (agent call): an HTTP API on localhost with a bearer token kept under `~/.ssh`, plus a `board` CLI that resolves the repo from the bead id prefix, never blocks or fails an agent (when the app is down it writes the event to the spooled-events table and exits 0; if Postgres is down too it prints a warning and exits 0; the app replays the table on boot), exits 3 with the allowed events on an out-of-order claim, and has `--json`. Observed events cannot be posted through the API.
12. **Skills integration** (user): in the MVP, as its last slices once the CLI is proven: `/tight-spec` and `/to-tickets` drive the epic machine; `dispatch` records sessions; the brief template has build sessions send `progress` and `report`; the coordinator's close-out sends `review`, `request_changes`, `commit`; a new `board` skill teaches the verbs. These are tickets in the skills repo, linked to this epic.
13. **Views** (user: epic-first; layout an agent call): the home view is **initiatives**: every epic across projects as a row with its stage (draft stages for ideas and specs, derived stages once ticketed), progress bar, ticket-stage histogram, fallout count and open change requests; draft epics sit at the top; one **Unplanned** lane at the bottom holds orphan tickets. Opening an epic shows its tickets on stage columns (columns from config: groups of ticket stages), planned and fallout shown apart, plus the blocking graph. Filters: project, type, label, beads status, stale badge. Ticket detail sheet (beads fields, stage, stage history, sessions, agent notes, linked CRs, allowed next events). CR panel per project (stack order, checks, links, merge action). Settings (config source, validation result, reload, repos found on disk but not configured, with a block to paste). Config columns validate against the ticket machine's states; epic stages are not configurable. **The mockup is revised to this layout and approved by the user before any view is built.**
14. **Bootstrap** (user): beads-board tracks its own build in beads during bootstrap, in its own repo initialised the house way (embedded store plus `issues.jsonl` export on every commit; bd 1.1 has no working store-less mode). The skills-repo tickets for Decision 12 name their beads-board parent in their description; cross-repo dependency edges are out of scope. Once the board runs, beads-board is an ordinary configured repo on it.

## Acceptance checks

1. Every configured beads repo appears (today's six plus beads-board); we_go_next_dev shows unreachable and the rest sync; ticket counts per repo equal `bd list --all` length at the same moment.
2. A `bd note` or `bd create` in form-engine shows on the board within 5 s without a reload (30 s if the probe forced the slower rule); an untouched repo costs no database writes on a sweep (hash skip, visible in logs).
2a. The probe's loop of agent-style `bd` writes (create, update, note, close) running against the live board on a scratch repo for 10 minutes has zero failed writes; the board's failed or skipped reads, if any, show only in its own logs.
2b. The initiatives view shows form-engine's fe-813 and fe-lwp as epic rows with derived stages and progress matching `bd`; a ticket with `discovered-from` under fe-813 shows as fallout under it; a ticket with no epic shows in Unplanned.

Running a real dispatch through the `dispatch` skill (fe-813.4 or the next ticket) moves its card to dispatched with window, branch and brief, then to building and reported as the pi session sends `progress` and `report`, then to in_review and committed as the coordinator closes out, with no manual `board` call by the user.
4. A claim out of order (`board review` on a queued ticket) exits 3 and prints the current stage and allowed events; the refused claim appears in the ticket's history as invalid.
5. With the app stopped, `board progress` exits 0 with a warning and its event sits in the spooled-events table; after start it applies and shows in history. With Postgres stopped too, it still exits 0 with a warning.

In the scratch forge repo, through the UI: merging the top of a two-CR stack is refused; merging the bottom produces a merge commit at the confirmed sha; the child is retargeted to the default branch; a moved head between confirm and merge is refused; the linked ticket goes to merged and the UI suggests the `bd close` command.
9. form-engine's real open PRs show in stack order with links to their beads, read-only, and no merge is possible on a CR whose base is not the default branch.

The repo tree contains no license material and no local operator path (`mix precommit` guard plus the global commit hook); the running board adds or changes no tracked file in any beads repo (`git status` in every configured repo before and after a day's use; planned skills-repo edits excluded). The app keeps no data outside Postgres apart from the config file and the token.

## Verification plan

- `mix precommit` (format, zero warnings, credo if adopted, tests) is the gate for every slice.
- Seams: the pure machines (`step/3`, compile-fail fixtures, generated-doc goldens, property tests over random event sequences); the beads reader (against scratch copies of real repos and a fixture export); the forge contract suite (fake forge in `mix test`; the GitHub adapter against recorded responses in `mix test` and live against the scratch repo when the adapter changes); LiveView tests for each view; the `board` CLI end to end against a running app.
- Outside the code: the real-dispatch walk-through (check 3), `git status` across all six repos (check 11), and screenshot review against the mockup (check 12).
- Concurrency probe (`bd export` loop against a loop of agent-style writes on a scratch copy of a repo) before the reader; its result and the chosen read rule are recorded in the repo's docs.

## Ask-first boundaries

- Creating the scratch forge repo on GitHub, or any other outward action (PRs, merges) outside it.
- Any write to a beads store or a beads repo, including hooks.
- Installing system software, systemd units, or touching dotfiles (the config file and env exports go in through the user or a dotfiles ticket).
- Adding a forge adapter beyond GitHub, or a feature outside Decisions 7–13.
- Changing the stage or epic machine's states or events beyond the tables above.
- Building any view before the revised mockup is approved.
- Any storage outside Postgres beyond the config file and the token.

## Left to the builder

- Schema details, module layout, Oban queue names and cron times within the stated bounds.
- Exact poll intervals and sweep timing, within "visible within 5 s" and "no writes when unchanged".
- CLI flag spelling and output format, keeping the verbs in Decision 7, 8 and 11.
- Fluxon component choice per view, staying within the mockup.
- Whether the `board` skill is one skill or folded into `dispatch`/`flow`, as long as each workflow step calls the verb.
